## What this course is

MA491 is an applied statistics course. The emphasis is on choosing a defensible
method, carrying it out correctly in R, and explaining the result to someone who
will act on it. Derivations appear where they change how you use a method, not
for their own sake.

## What you should be able to do by the end

- Frame a practical question as a statistical one, and say what the data would
  have to look like for your answer to be wrong.
- Fit, check, and interpret the standard models covered in the course.
- Carry an analysis end to end in R, from raw data to a written conclusion.
- Read a published analysis critically enough to find its weak point.

## Materials

- **Software:** [R](https://cran.r-project.org) and
  [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/). Both free.
- **Textbook:** *to be set by the course director.*

## Grading

| Component | Weight |
|---|---:|
| Homework | 20% |
| Projects | 25% |
| WPRs | 35% |
| Final | 20% |
| **Total** | **100%** |

## Getting help

Every instructor holds office hours; see the [People](people/index.qmd) page.
Additional instruction is expected, not remedial — come early rather than the
night before something is due.

## Academic integrity

Work you submit must be yours. Collaboration on homework is encouraged as long
as you write your own solution and document who you worked with. Graded events
are individual unless stated otherwise. *Full documentation policy to be added
by the course director.*
